As an IT Specialist (System Analysis) "Product Manager", GS-2210-15, you will be responsible for: Leading the definition and evolution of FSA products by understanding the needs of students, families, and stakeholders, translating insights into prioritized product roadmaps, and ensuring product decisions improve access to aid and simplify the user experience.

Serving as the bridge between policy goals, technical systems, and user needs by translating complex constraints into actionable requirements and ensuring solutions meet compliance and security standards while delivering user-friendly experiences at national scale.

Directing and aligning contractors and partner agencies to support the product vision, holding vendors accountable for outcomes, and fostering collaboration across engineering, design, policy, and operations teams to deliver a coherent, high-quality FSA experience.

Connecting day-to-day work to the mission of expanding educational opportunity, fostering a product culture centered on experimentation, data-driven decision-making, and continuous improvement, and providing vision that aligns government staff and vendors around shared goals for students and families.

Applying deep experience building and managing products at scale to ensure FSA systems deliver secure, reliable, and seamless experiences while protecting sensitive data and maintaining public trust.
Minimum Qualification Requirements You may meet the minimum qualifications for the GS-15, if you possess the specialize experience.

Specialized Experience for the GS-15: One year of experience in either federal or non-federal service that is equivalent to at least a GS-14 performing two (2) out of three (3) of the following duties or work assignments: Experience serving as the product leader in the development of a scaled technology platform.

Experience serving as a product manager, overseeing internal and external software development, testing, integration, and operation. Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and translating business requirements into technical user stories.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) The quality of your experience will be measured by the extent to which you possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs).

You do not need to provide separate narrative responses to these KSAs, as they will be measured by your responses to the occupational questionnaire (you may preview the occupational questionnaire by clicking the link at the end of the Evaluations section of this vacancy announcement).

Knowledge of product management principles, with a focus on user-centered design and measurable outcomes. Skill in translating policy and technical requirements into intuitive, scalable product solutions. Skill in managing vendors and cross-functional teams to deliver results and drive tangible product improvements.

Ability to inspire and sustain a mission-driven product culture. Knowledge of building and operating large-scale, mission-critical systems or comparable technology infrastructure.

Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. We are trusted by 300+ million people in 100+ countries for our industry-leading security, user fund transparency, trading engine speed, deep liquidity, and an unmatched portfolio of digital-asset products.

Binance offerings range from trading and finance to education, research, payments, institutional services, Web3 features, and more. We leverage the power of digital assets and blockchain to build an inclusive financial ecosystem to advance the freedom of money and improve financial access for people around the world.

Responsibilities: Work directly with merchants and PSP partners to guide them through the full integration lifecycle, from solution design and API integration to testing, go-live, and post-launch support. Lead technical discussions with merchant product and engineering teams to design optimal integration approaches using Binance payment solutions.

Act as the primary liaison between merchants, product managers, and engineering teams to ensure smooth communication and efficient problem solving. Provide hands-on support during merchant integrations, helping troubleshoot technical issues and ensuring a high integration success rate.

Educate merchants on integration best practices, API usage, and optimal payment flows for both web and mobile environments. Support merchants in designing effective checkout experiences and payment UI/UX to improve end-user conversion and payment success rates.

Conduct integration testing with merchants and internal teams to validate payment flows and ensure readiness for launch. Analyze merchant feedback, performance data, and market trends to identify opportunities to improve Binance payment products and integration tools.

Collaborate with product teams to close functionality gaps and propose enhancements that improve merchant integration experience. Engage with merchants regularly to understand their needs, gather insights, and help optimize their payment integration over time.

Requirements: 5+ years of experience in payment integrations, fintech, or merchant-facing technical roles Experience working with payment gateways, PSPs, or merchant payment solutions Strong understanding of REST APIs and integration workflows Ability to work directly with merchant product or engineering teams to guide technical integrations Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders Experience coordinating cross-functional teams across product, engineering, and business Familiarity with web or mobile technologies (JavaScript, Node.js, HTML5, Java, Python, etc.) is a plus Knowledge in crypto or Web3 payment infrastructure is a strong advantage Why Binance
· Shape the future with the world’s leading blockchain ecosystem
· Collaborate with world-class talent in a user-centric global organization with a flat structure
· Tackle unique, fast-paced projects with autonomy in an innovative environment
· Thrive in a results-driven workplace with opportunities for career growth and continuous learning
· Competitive salary and company benefits
· Work-from-home arrangement (the arrangement may vary depending on the work nature of the business team) Binance is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We believe that having a diverse workforce is fundamental to our success. By submitting a job application, you confirm that you have read and agree to our Candidate Privacy Notice . deine aufgaben: Bei chargecloud bauen wir das digitale Herzstück der europäischen Ladeinfrastruktur für Elektrofahrzeuge.

Unser cloudbasiertes Ökosystem – mit dem chargecloud Operating System im Zentrum, erweitert durch Whitelabel-Frontends und Partner-Services – ermöglicht es E-Mobility-Helden, ihr Lade-Business aufzubauen und zu skalieren, kWh für kWh. Zur Verstärkung unserer wachsenden Produktorganisation suchen wir eine:n Product Owner.

Dein zukünftiger Aufgabenbereich könnte nah an der Customer Experience, dem kommerziellen und finanziellen Rückgrat oder dem technischen und datenbasierten Fundament unserer Plattform liegen – die optimale Passform definieren wir gemeinsam im Recruiting-Prozess. Übernimm die volle Verantwortung für deinen Produktbereich – von der Discovery über die Delivery bis hin zu messbaren Ergebnissen Verantworte und pflege das Product Backlog und priorisiere eigenständig auf Basis von Produktstrategie, Kundennutzen sowie Aufwand/Risiko Betreibe kontinuierliche Product Discovery: Sprich regelmäßig mit Kunden sowie Nutzern, validiere Probleme und Lösungen frühzeitig und teste Konzepte, bevor du sie skalierst Definiere und verfeinere Anforderungen gemeinsam mit Engineering Leads und Stakeholdern; übersetze komplexe geschäftliche, regulatorische oder technische Themen in klare Deliverables und messbare Ergebnisse Pflege und kommuniziere eine ergebnisorientierte Roadmap, die Innovation, Kundenbedürfnisse und Plattformstabilität in Einklang bringt Nutze Daten und Produktmetriken, um Entscheidungen zu treffen, Erfolge zu messen und zu iterieren – nicht nur für das Reporting Arbeite in unserer Product-Development-Organisation und liefere iterativ neue Funktionen, während du bestehende kontinuierlich verbesserst das bist du: Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager in einem SaaS-Umfeld.

Nachgewiesene Fähigkeit, komplexe Backlogs zu managen und zwischen geschäftlichen, kundenbezogenen und technischen Anforderungen zu vermitteln. Praktische Erfahrung mit modernen Methoden der Produktentwicklung – Continuous Discovery, iterative Delivery, ergebnisorientiertes Roadmapping und evidenzbasierte Priorisierung.

Du definierst Erfolgsmetriken, arbeitest mit Produktanalysen und lässt dich bei deinen Entscheidungen von Fakten und Daten leiten. Du nutzt schon heute aktiv KI-Tools in deiner täglichen Arbeit und denkst darüber nach, wie KI sowohl Produkte als auch Prozesse verbessern kann. Du verstehst, wie moderne Softwareplattformen funktionieren (z. B.

APIs, Integrationen, Cloud-Architekturen), und kannst in Diskussionen mit Engineers auf Augenhöhe argumentieren. Exzellente Kommunikations- und Stakeholder-Management-Fähigkeiten gegenüber technischem und nicht-technischem Publikum.

Du sprichst fließend Englisch; Deutschkenntnisse sind ein Plus. das bieten wir: Remote First: Ob Homeoffice, deutschlandweite Coworking Spaces oder moderne Zentrale in Köln – wir decken alle Arbeitsformen ab. Gut ausgestattet: Damit es dir im Homeoffice an nichts fehlt, stellen wir die passende Hardware zur Verfügung.

Nach der Probezeit erhältst du zusätzlich ein Budget für ergonomisches Arbeiten von zu Hause. Flexibilität: Bei uns kannst du deine Arbeitszeit flexibel gestalten: Mit einer Kernarbeitszeit von 9:00 bis 12:00 Uhr hast du Freiraum, um Beruf und Privatleben entspannt zu vereinen.

Mit unserem Workation Worldwide Programm kannst du bis zu 60 Arbeitstage im Jahr ortsunabhängig arbeiten – jetzt weltweit innerhalb von ±4 Stunden zur deutschen Zeitzone.

Benefits à la carte: Mit Probonio gestaltest du deine Benefits jeden Monat neu: Nutze dein Budget für Essenszuschüsse, Kita-Zuschüsse, Gutscheine oder buche dein Urban Sports Club Abo – ganz flexibel per App. Erholung & Auszeit : Du profitierst von 32 Tagen bezahltem Urlaub pro Jahr.

Zusätzlich sind Heiligabend und Silvester bei uns komplett arbeitsfrei. Mit unserem Culture Day kannst du dir außerdem einen Tag freinehmen, der dir persönlich wichtig ist – ganz bewusst und individuell.

Unternehmensweiter Bonus: Unser Shared Success Plan fördert den gemeinsamen Fokus auf unsere Ziele, indem wir den Erfolg unseres Unternehmens transparent und fair mit allen teilen. Mobilität & Nachhaltigkeit: Über FINN JobAuto kannst du dein eigenes E-Fahrzeug zu attraktiven Konditionen leasen. Zusätzlich profitierst du von Bikeleasing.

Teamgeist: Unsere Teams treffen sich einmal im Tertial persönlich zu Brainstorming, Workshops und natürlich zu unseren beliebten Sommer- und Winterfeiern. Gesund im Job: Wir unterstützen dich mit Urban Sports Club, Life Coaching Programmen und weiteren Angeboten, damit du fit und stressfrei durch den Arbeitsalltag kommst.

Agentic AI ist deine Welt – und du willst dich damit beschäftigen, statt ständig etwas verkaufen zu müssen?
Du hast dich intensiv mit KI-Agenten beschäftigt, eigene Workflows oder Anwendungen gebaut und kennst Themen wie n8n, Make, APIs, Tool Calling, RAG, Vektordatenbanken oder MCP aus der Praxis?
Dann bau mit uns den besten Agentic-AI-Kurs im deutschsprachigen Raum.
Aufgaben
Der Titel heißt Product Manager – gemeint ist aber jemand, der Lerninhalte baut, nichtverwaltet: halb Instructional Designer, halb Agentic-AI-Bastler. Du gestaltest das Produkt „Kurs“, von der ersten Demo bis zum fertigen Modul. Dabei beschäftigst du dich mit uns zusammen unter anderem mit folgenden Fragen:
Was müssen Menschen heute über Agentic AI wissen?
Welche Tools, Modelle und Frameworks sind wirklich relevant?
Welche Agenten und Automatisierungen sollten Teil des Kurses sein?
Wie lassen sich technische Inhalte verständlich und praxisnah vermitteln?
Welche Übungen, Projekte und Demos bringen Teilnehmer wirklich weiter?
Du unterstützt uns dabei, Inhalte zu strukturieren, praktische Anwendungen zu bauen, Lernmaterialien zu entwickeln und Referenten fachlich zu begleiten. Einzelne Inhalte kannst du später auch selbst unterrichten.
Qualifikation
Wir suchen keinen Verkäufer und keinen klassischen Bildungsmanager – sondern jemanden mit technischem Hintergrund, der bereits tief in Agentic AI steckt, neue Entwicklungen aufmerksam verfolgt und komplexe Dinge verständlich erklären kann.
Ob Berufseinsteiger mit starkem Portfolio oder mit ein paar Jahren Erfahrung in Content, Training oder Produktentwicklung – entscheidend ist, was du bereits gebaut oder vermittelt hast, nicht dein Titel.

Kleines Team, kurze Wege
Hybrides Arbeits-Setup: Büro in Berlin-Mitte + Homeoffice
Tägliche Arbeit mit den aktuellsten KI-Tools und -Entwicklungen
Echte Verantwortung ab Tag 1 - du verwaltest nicht, du baust auf
Perspektive auf eine wachsende Rolle in einem wachsenden Bereich
Vollzeit, unbefristet.
Schick uns nicht nur deinen Lebenslauf – zeig uns, womit du dich beschäftigst und was du bereits gebaut oder entwickelt hast (z.B. Kurskonzepte, Workshops, Tutorials oder Prototypen)!

Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta ’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel.

The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day. Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia.

Cresta ’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu , founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences. Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day.

Come build that future at Cresta . About the Role As our first EMEA Forward Deployed Product Manager, AI Agent , you will create, deploy and optimize AI Agents that transform our customers’ businesses and delight their customers.

This highly cross-functional and customer-facing role blends product thinking, a nose for value, and project leadership with senior customer executives. At the end of the day, you own each AI Agent and the outcomes they drive for our customers, and you take that personally.

You are a creative, pragmatic problem solver who thrives in fast-paced environments, rolls up your sleeves to build, and excels at turning ambiguity into execution. In this role, you’ll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who will support the build, integrations and optimization to make each AI Agent successful.

You’ll also work closely with product and engineering, providing a tight feedback loop and custom tooling that will shape the future of our platform. As the first hire in EMEA, you’ll also play a key role in setting the standards for the role in the EMEA region and helping to grow the team as we scale.

What You’ll Do Own AI Agent outcomes for our customers — defining and delivering on the metrics that move the needle. This includes finding additional automation opportunities that can provide even more value!

To do this, you’ll… Own the deployment lifecycle for AI Agents — from scoping and kickoff to launch and post-go-live optimization Design, build, test and iterate on AI agents in partnership with FDEs using Cresta ’s internal tools and the latest technologies to deliver the highest customer ROI Serve as the AI Agent SME for the EMEA Sales cycle, partnering on demos, solutioning, and deal reviews to ensure technical feasibility, value articulation, and successful handoff to deployment.

Lead customer relationships and act as the primary point of contact for AI Agent. Help customers move faster to ensure we can deliver quickly and effectively.

Facilitate workshops and design sessions with customer stakeholders to align on agent use cases, workflows, and success criteria Work closely with FDEs to ensure smooth implementation, build new capabilities as needed and provide feedback and improvements to our broader platform Improve our playbooks for agent development and customer deployment Build our forward deployed practice for EMEA, setting the standards for future growth What We’re Looking For 5+ years of experience in Technology Consulting, Implementations, Product, or Customer Success roles, ideally working closely with AI or LLM first products Hands-on work style – curiosity with a bias for action.

You anticipate needs and bottlenecks and deliver with urgency and care.

Experience leading complex deployments, owning customer relationships (including senior customer stakeholders), and working cross-functionally Strong technical understanding, systems thinking and exposure to building Agents (not necessarily conversational, personal projects count!) Comfortable working with ambiguity and learning quickly in a dynamic startup environment Passion for AI, automation, and shaping the future of customer experience Bonus Points Background in product management, conversation design or forward deployed engineering roles Experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment Familiarity with customer support and contact center operations Perks & Benefits: We offer a comprehensive and people-first benefits package to support you at work and in life: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with plans to fit you and your family Paid parental leave for all new parents welcoming a new child Remote work setup budget to help you create a productive home office Monthly wellness and communication stipend to keep you connected and balanced 20 days of vacation time Compensation at Cresta Cresta ’s approach to compensation is simple: recognize impact, reward excellence, and invest in our people.

We offer competitive, location-based pay that reflects the market and what each individual brings to the table. Final offers are shaped by factors like experience, skills, education, and geography. In addition to base pay, total compensation includes equity and a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family.

We have noticed a rise in recruiting impersonations across the industry, where scammers attempt to access candidates' personal and financial information through fake interviews and offers. All Cresta recruiting email communications will always come from the @cresta.ai domain.

Any outreach claiming to be from Cresta via other sources should be ignored. If you are uncertain whether you have been contacted by an official Cresta employee, reach out to recruiting@cresta.ai Originally posted on Himalayas

We are building a SaaS platform that packages Autodesk Consulting’s intellectual property — proven workflows, implementation guidance, learning content, and tooling recommendations — into a scalable digital experience that connects customers and internal Autodesk consultants to the knowledge they need to drive successful digital transformation. This is a platform built at the intersection of knowledge management, content delivery, and AI-assisted discovery, and it is evolving rapidly.
As Senior Principal Product Manager, you will own the full platform — the foundation on which our Solutions, Services, and advisory experiences are built.

You will define and drive the product vision and roadmap, work directly with lead architects and engineering teams across India and Poland, partner closely with our UI/UX designer, and collaborate with Product Owners who manage sprint-level delivery across multiple scrum teams.

You will also serve as the connective tissue between three critical stakeholder groups: the customers and Autodesk consultants who use the platform daily, and the Solutions and Services PMs who have a stake in how their content and services are experienced and consumed.
This is a role for someone who is energized by building. The platform is new, the market opportunity is significant, and the roadmap reflects that ambition. The person in this role will thrive on creating structure in a fast-moving environment, making high-quality decisions with incomplete information, and shaping a product that is still defining what it can become.

Own the end-to-end product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the platform, balancing near-term delivery with long-term platform integrity
Define and drive the AI-assisted discovery and personalization strategy that enables customers and consultants to find relevant workflows, solutions, and knowledge based on their specific context
Partner with lead architects and senior engineers across globally distributed teams to translate product strategy into technical direction
Work with Product Owners to ensure roadmap priorities are effectively executed across multiple scrum teams
Collaborate with Solutions and Services PMs to ensure platform capabilities effectively support content delivery and service consumption experiences
Develop deep understanding of the needs of both external customers and internal Autodesk consultants, and translate those needs into platform features and experiences
Define and track success metrics that reflect both platform health and the business outcomes the platform is designed to drive
Navigate a complex stakeholder environment, building alignment across consulting leadership, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams
Contribute to the commercialization strategy, helping define how the platform creates and captures value over time

10+ years of product management experience, with a track record of shipping complex, multi-stakeholder products
Demonstrated experience building AI-enabled applications, particularly in the areas of intelligent search, contextual discovery, recommendation systems, or personalization
Experience building products that span SaaS applications, content platforms, and service delivery — not just traditional software features
Proven ability to operate effectively in early-stage or rapidly evolving product environments where structure and clarity must be created, not inherited
Strong technical fluency, with the ability to engage meaningfully with architects and engineers on system design, data architecture, and AI/ML approaches
Experience working with globally distributed engineering teams
Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence without authority at a senior level
Nice to have: experience building content lifecycle management products, particularly those involving structured, hierarchical, or reusable content — including authoring, publishing workflows, versioning, and change propagation
AI/ML frameworks and application patterns, including RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), vector databases, semantic search, and large language model integration
Modern SaaS platform architecture and API-driven product design
Content management and knowledge management systems
Content lifecycle management tooling, including structured authoring environments, library management, and publishing workflows
Analytics and data pipeline tooling
Agile delivery methodologies and experience working with Product Owners across multiple scrum teams
The Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate has built products where an intelligent discovery layer is the differentiator — where the ability to surface the right knowledge, in the right context, for the right user is what makes the product worth using. They understand what it takes to make that experience feel effortless, and they bring the technical depth to engage meaningfully with engineers and architects on how to build it.
They are comfortable in the ambiguity of a brand new product. They don’t need a mature backlog or a well-worn playbook — they can create structure where none exists, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and keep a complex roadmap moving without losing sight of the long-term vision.
They think in systems. They understand that a platform serving customers, internal consultants, and peer product managers simultaneously requires architectural thinking, not just feature thinking.
They are a natural connector. In a role that sits at the center of platform, solutions, and services, they build trust quickly, communicate with clarity, and have a track record of aligning diverse stakeholders around a shared direction.
A candidate who also brings experience with content lifecycle management — structured authoring, library systems, versioning, and hierarchical content relationships — would bring a rare and particularly valuable perspective to this role.

Bring complex customer and technical problems to life, inspiring and aligning senior leadership and the broader organization around your vision. Execute with Excellence: Conduct thorough opportunity assessments, backed by data and customer research, to validate assumptions and prioritize initiatives.

Exceptional Communicator: You possess outstanding written and verbal communication skills and are seen as an expert storyteller. Strategic Impact: You will be driving the foundation of Cint 's current and future success. Innovation: You will be on the cutting edge of ResTech and data technology, solving novel problems with a world-class R&D team. Ownership: We empower our product team. You will have the autonomy and accountability to make a measurable impact on the business. Our Values Collaboration is our superpower We uncover rich perspectives across the world Success happens together We deliver across borders.

Innovation is in our blood We’re pioneers in our industry Our curiosity is insatiable We bring the best ideas to life. We do what we say We’re accountable for our work and actions Excellence comes as standard We’re open, honest and kind, always.

We are caring We learn from each other’s experiences Stop and listen; every opinion matters We embrace diversity, equity and inclusion. Cint Group AB (publ), listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, this growth has made Cint a strong global platform with teams across its many global offices, including Stockholm, London, New York, New Orleans, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney.

(www.cint.com) Additionally, in a world of AI, we want our candidates to understand our approach to the use of AI during the interview and hiring process, so we'd appreciate you reading our AI usage guide . Who We Are Cint is a pioneer in research technology (ResTech).

Our customers use the Cint platform to post questions and get answers from real people to build business strategies, confidently publish research, accurately measure the impact of digital advertising, and more.

The Cint platform is built on a programmatic marketplace, which is the world’s largest, with nearly 300 million respondents in over 130 countries. At Cint , we are committed to innovation and are rapidly expanding our portfolio of data solutions to power the next generation of insights.

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).
AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.
Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

As a Senior Product Manager, you own whether the solution is valuable to customers and viable for the business, working alongside design and engineering, who bring usability and feasibility. This role needs to build strong working relationships across design and engineering and pull in the right partners for the problem at hand.

It also needs a working knowledge of the constraints across marketing, sales, customer success, finance, accounting, legal, and privacy, plus a deep understanding of who our athletes are and how they actually use our products.

That depth comes from genuine curiosity: about the business, about the families and athletes we serve, about the data behind their behavior, and about the technology, including AI, that shapes what's possible for the product.

The best person for this this role builds shared context across the teams around them, and earns trust and rapport with stakeholders, not through authority, but by consistently showing up with the right questions and the right evidence. This role sits at the bleeding edge of solving problems for families navigating the college recruiting process.

The decisions made here will shape the experience for thousands of families, and in some cases change the course of a young athlete's life. It's an individual contributor role, accountable for solving real problems for customers in a way that works for the business, not just shipping a list of features.

Success here is measured by the outcomes we create for athletes and families, and by how those outcomes move the business forward.

Execute against and help inform the product vision and strategy for the Core Athlete experience, translating it into a roadmap where each phase of work builds on the one before it, not just a queue of features. Foster shared understanding of that vision and strategy across your team and stakeholders.
Build and maintain deep, current knowledge of the business, our athletes and families, the data behind their behavior, and the technology behind our products, and use that knowledge to spot the right problems early.
Own the backlog. Write user stories and acceptance criteria that make the “why” clear, not just the “what.”
Partner with design and engineering, and pull in the right people across the business, to move from discovery to delivery.
Run experiments to test solutions before betting the roadmap on them. Feasibility and usability get tested early, not discovered late.
Track industry trends and the competitive landscape in athlete recruiting, and bring that context back to the team.
Stay fluent in AI as it evolves. Spot where it can change the product for athletes and families, and use it to speed up your own research, analysis, and daily workflow.
Build trust and rapport with stakeholders across Marketing, Sales, Operations, and Support. Use data and a clear narrative, not just authority, to align people around decisions.
Stay accountable for the metrics behind the roadmap, not just the delivery schedule.

5+ years of product management experience, ideally including consumer-facing or user-facing products on a sprint-based, cross-functional team.
Demonstrated ability to run product discovery: framing problems, testing solutions with real users, and killing ideas that don't hold up.
Working SQL skills. You should be comfortable pulling and interpreting your own data rather than waiting on someone else's report.
Experience partnering directly with engineers and designers as peers to move ideas from discovery to delivery.
Genuine curiosity about the business, the customer, the data, and the technology, and the judgment to know which one matters most for a given problem.
AI fluency: comfortable using AI tools day to day, and sharp enough about what AI can and can't do to spot where it genuinely changes the product.
A track record of turning ambiguous, cross-functional problems into a clear, prioritized backlog.
Proven track record of translating complex business needs into clear product strategies and roadmaps.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills. You should be able to write a one-page narrative that convinces a skeptical exec, and influence and align senior stakeholders, not just present a slide deck that restates numbers.
Highly self-motivated and resourceful, comfortable leading both strategy and execution.
Experience working in Agile/Scrum development environments.
Comfortable holding a position and defending it with data, while staying genuinely open to being wrong.

An Introduction to Primer
Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.
Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.
Watch our showcase >
Read up on our $100m Series C

Which team will you be joining?
Getting paid is only half the story. Understanding and managing those payments is where the real work begins.
In the Financial Operations team we build the tools and infrastructure that let merchants take control of their payments: reconciling funds, monitoring performance, and automating the operations that keep everything running. We also own Global Accounts, giving merchants the ability to hold, manage and move funds across currencies and markets, a foundational capability as Primer expands into more complex, cross-border payment environments.
The team spans Reconciliation, Operations Automation, Global Accounts and FX. As a Product Manager here you will own a sub-area within that: a coherent slice of the product where you own the problems, the prioritisation and the outcomes over multiple quarters.
You will work day to day with a dedicated engineering team and design partner, alongside GTM, and report into the Product lead for the area. Primer is remote-first and globally distributed, and always will be. We run on written thinking, low bureaucracy and real ownership. You build it, you own it, end to end.
What will you be doing?
Owning the outcomes for your sub-area of Financial Operations over multiple quarters, not just shipping a backlog
Defining the problems worth solving in your scope by synthesising merchant feedback, support data, competitive moves and platform constraints
Planning and delivering initiatives independently, making real-time trade-offs on scope, sequencing and quality to protect both timelines and outcomes
Writing specs that anticipate the edge cases that actually matter in payments operations: reconciliation breaks, currency and settlement complexity
Partnering closely with engineering on feasibility and technical trade-offs, and defining the leading and lagging metrics that tell you whether your sub-area is working
Owning launch readiness and driving rapid post-launch iteration based on what the data shows
Representing your sub-area to merchants and internal stakeholders, turning operational complexity into clear product decisions

A track record of owning a product sub-area or significant feature set end to end, with outcomes that can be traced back to your decisions
The ability to define problems independently from messy inputs, rather than waiting for a fully formed brief
Sound, autonomous trade-offs on scope, quality and technical debt within your scope
Enough technical fluency to partner with engineers on feasibility and integration implications, not just hand over requirements
Clear, structured communication that keeps engineering, design and GTM aligned and surfaces risks early

Experience in payments, fintech, or operational and back-office product such as reconciliation, ledgers, treasury or FX
Comfort with data analysis to define and track outcome metrics
You may not like it here
Financial operations is detail-heavy and unforgiving. Reconciliation and FX have real money and real edge cases attached. If you prefer broad, abstract product work to getting the details exactly right, this will frustrate you.
You are expected to define what is worth solving in your sub-area, with support rather than direction.
We are remote-first and async by default. If you need people physically around you to do your best work, this is a real adjustment, not a perk.
Feedback here is direct and frequent. You are expected to give it as well as take it.

What's the culture like at Primer?
We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants.
We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities.
The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone.

Senior Product Manager — Manifest
About Manifest
Manifest is building modern software for the tours and activities industry.
Our customers run real-world businesses: tours, attractions, experiences, rentals, and activities. They need software that helps them sell more, operate smoothly, and deliver great guest experiences.
We're building a B2B2C SaaS platform that brings booking, ecommerce, payments, accounting, operations, and customer experience together in a modern architecture. The product surface is broad, the workflows are nuanced, and the opportunity is big.

That surface now spans several distinct product areas, including a newer, AI-native platform for building and delivering customer websites end-to-end. We're hiring more than one Senior Product Manager, and we'll match each hire to the area where their strengths fit best, from established features to fast-moving, zero-to-one greenfield work.
We're looking for Senior Product Managers to own product direction, roadmap, and prioritization for one or more key areas of Manifest.
This is not a backlog management role. We're looking for someone who can take ambiguous customer and business problems, find the shape of the opportunity, make smart tradeoffs, and help a cross-functional team ship high-quality product experiences.

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll turn customer insight, business context, and technical possibilities into clear product direction and own the delivery end-to-end.
Modern product work is changing, and this role reflects that. We expect our PMs to be fluent and genuinely enthusiastic users of AI-assisted tools—using Claude, Cursor, v0, and similar tools to explore interactions, build lightweight prototypes, and make product ideas concrete before implementation begins. On some of our teams, AI-native workflows are not just a way of working faster; they're central to the product itself.
You'll work closely with Product leadership, Engineering, customer-facing teams, and design-minded front-end engineers. Depending on the area you own, there may not be a dedicated product designer, so you should be comfortable playing an active role in shaping user workflows, interaction patterns, and overall product quality.
You'll also be the bridge between executive vision and execution: taking high-level direction set by our leadership team and honing it into concrete, buildable product requirements. Leadership helps frame the why and the what, but you own the product decisions about what to build and how to bring it to life.
You do not need to be a front-end engineer, and you won't be expected to write production code. But strong technical fluency is a real advantage—enough to collaborate deeply with engineers on UI-heavy, technically nuanced product areas, and to understand the systems you're shaping. A technical or former engineering background is strongly preferred.
You should also be comfortable owning the delivery side of the work, along with the product vision, like milestones, sequencing, and keeping a small team moving.

How We Work
We move quickly, but we care about craft.
Manifest serves users with complex day-to-day workflows, so product quality matters. We care about whether the product makes sense, whether the workflow is intuitive, whether the edge cases are handled thoughtfully, and whether the experience feels modern and trustworthy.
We value product managers who are curious, direct, clear-thinking, and outcome-oriented. We are not looking for someone who simply collects requirements or manages tickets. We're looking for someone who can understand customer problems, shape direction, make tradeoffs, and partner with Engineering from ambiguity through delivery and iteration.

s.h: Your Mission This is a company built for growth, not comfort.
s.t:
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.
We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.
Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform.

Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users.

At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.
If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.
What You’ll Own: Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.
What Success Looks Like: You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.
What You Bring Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.
How We Win Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.
Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

TL;DR — alago brings AI-powered project management to the construction industry. As our Product Manager , you'll own a core product area end to end: how messy project data becomes an early warning that a €200M project is about to go wrong. Full-time, Munich.
About alago
Imagine if building a building were as easy as building software. Every moving part visible, every change traceable, every decision still carrying its reasoning six months later.
Software got there by making its own history legible — every commit, every diff. Construction never did. A €200M project runs on plan sets nobody can diff and decisions buried in email, so the same mistakes happen over and over, and the industry loses $1.6 trillion a year to it.
That's what we're fixing. Eleven people, 15+ customers, €1M+ pre-seed from leading construction-tech VCs and one of Germany's largest project developers. The product is live and used daily on real construction sites — which means the interesting work is only starting.
Tasks

Translate deeply technical construction workflows into decisions engineers can build from
Own a product area end to end: From discovery on site to shipped, instrumented, measured features
Shape the roadmap: Balance what the next customer needs against the foundations that make the next ten cheap
Make the hard prioritization calls on scope and sequencing, and defend them
Define what "working" means: pick the metrics, instrument them, read production data, iterate
Treat LLM behavior as a product problem, not a research one — evals, fallbacks, and what the user sees when the model is wrong

2+ years shipping product — as a product manager, or as a UI/product designer who's been making product calls and not just screens
You've shipped something where the hard part was the data model, not the button
Hands-on experience with LLM-powered features in production — you know what breaks and how users react when it does
Genuine willingness to put on boots and go on site until you know the domain better than we do
Bonus
AEC background

You already build your own agents and internal tools to do your job faster

Heidi is building an AI Care Partner that supports clinicians every step of the way, from documentation to delivery of care.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people.

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to be the primary product voice for Elastic Security's most strategic enterprise customers. Solid products are built on a clear knowledge of real customer needs. In large enterprise accounts, those needs arrive as a constant stream of enhancement requests, feature asks, and hard problems.

They often arrive faster than any one team can act on them. Someone has to bring order to that stream, tell apart what a customer wants from what a customer needs, and turn it into a coherent product direction across different product areas.
In this high-impact role, you will own the relationship between Elastic Security's product organization and our most strategic enterprise accounts. You will manage enhancement requests across many enterprise customers at once.

You will prioritize them with judgment and data, and make sure they keep transitioning through the system instead of sitting idle.

You will be the person a CISO trusts in the room, the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and the person who can tell a major customer that something will not be built without losing the relationship.

You will work at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Engineering, building the structure that lets Elastic scale close customer relationships without simply adding headcount.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the enhancement request pipeline across multiple strategic enterprise accounts at once. Build and maintain a structured system to track, prioritize, and respond to customer-sourced requirements, and keep requests moving rather than leaving them in “under consideration.”
Translate customer requirements into shipped products. Work at the level of customer pain, not just the feature that was asked for, and synthesize input from many accounts into a single, coherent product direction.
Turn input from strategic accounts into successful products. Look for patterns across accounts. Shape some of these patterns into formal partnerships for design. Make sure the resulting capabilities benefit the wider market, not just the single customer that made the request.
Feed validated customer patterns back into the core product roadmaps, influencing direction well beyond the accounts you cover.
Serve as the primary product voice in meetings with senior customer stakeholders, including the CISO, CTO, and VP of Security Operations. Deliver roadmap updates, including deprioritizations and misses, in a way that keeps the relationship deep.
Prioritize customer-sourced requirements using structured frameworks such as RICE, weighted scoring, and opportunity sizing. Use data where it is available and clear judgment where it is thin, and be transparent about which is which.
Partner with product and engineering leads to write requirements they can act on without follow-up clarification meetings. Understand system architecture well enough to assess feasibility and scope on your own.
Operate across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Legal. Support deal cycles as a product resource through RFP responses, security questionnaires, and roadmap presentations to prospects.
Navigate tension between a customer's contractual expectations and the internal roadmap , and tackle it directly rather than through routine escalation.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers, enhancement request dashboards, and decision memos that give customers and internal stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.
Advocate for customer needs inside the company while resisting the pull of the loudest or largest customer setting the roadmap at the expense of the broader market.

Extensive Experience: 7–10 years of product management experience, with at least 4 years in B2B enterprise software. A consistent record of owning a product area with meaningful revenue impact and of leading products from customer input through shipped, iterated outcomes. Direct experience working with named strategic accounts, not only through customer success proxies. Experience with hyperscalers, MSSPs and/or PubSec is a solid plus.
Security Domain Knowledge: Hands-on knowledge with SIEM, SOAR, XDR or broader security operations platforms, either as a product manager or as a practitioner such as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or security architect.

You can credibly discuss detection engineering, log ingestion pipelines, correlation rules, threat hunting workflows, and compliance use cases without a solutions engineer in the room. You understand the difference between what a CISO wants to hear and what a SOC analyst actually needs.

A background as a security practitioner, such as SOC, incident response, or detection engineering, before moving into product is a solid plus, and brings credibility that is hard to teach.
Enhancement Request Management at Scale: You have personally run a structured enhancement request pipeline across several enterprise accounts at the same time. You can step into a relationship with dozens of open requests and no prior documentation and build a working tracking system within weeks.
Executive Presence: You are comfortable as the primary product voice with C-suite and VP-level customer stakeholders. You can deliver difficult news without losing the relationship, and you can hold both the executive view and the analyst view in the same meeting.
Technical Credibility: You earn respect from engineering through the quality of your requirements rather than through authority. You write specs engineers can act on, and you know enough about architecture to judge feasibility and scope.
Cross-functional Leadership and Influence: You have operated at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, and Legal, and you know which function owns what and how to advance work across all of them. You lead across a matrixed organization, align multiple stakeholders toward a common vision, and drive execution in a dynamic, remote-first environment, with the autonomy and judgment expected of a principal-level product leader.
Structured Thinking and Bias for Closure: You bring order to unstructured problems, using data to prioritize and clear judgment when data is thin, and staying transparent about which is which. You move work through the system and follow up proactively rather than waiting to be asked, defaulting to visibility through artifacts instead of meetings. You advocate for customer needs while synthesizing them into product direction rather than relaying demands.

(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3)
The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. Now we need a PM who wants to take that further, in a market being rewritten in real time.
Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. Nobody has really figured out what reliability means for this kind of software yet. That's the problem you'd own.
As a Product Manager, you will be responsible for empowering developers and designers to solve customer problems. You will work directly with our SVP Product Engineering Daniel .

Shape company and product strategy alongside our SVP of Product Engineering. It's a genuine partnership: you'll develop the vision for where Checkly goes next, decide where we play in the AI testing, monitoring, and observability landscape and where we don't, and turn that into a direction. You build the strategy with us, not execute someone else's.
Shape Checkly's point of view on reliability in an AI-native world: how teams monitor AI-generated code, agent-driven workflows, and LLM-backed features
Lead initiatives across Product Engineering, Sales and Marketing, and represent Checkly directly to customers and in developer communities.
Live in the product and the problem. Empathy for DevOps, SRE and Platform Engineering isn't a line item. It's the job.
You ship with AI where it helps and know when not to. You don't just talk about it.
What you should have
You've built software before this. You're an ex-engineer, ex-founder, or ex-solutions engineer who has written real code and shipped real things, and now you want to own the product. This one's non-negotiable: you should be able to reason about APIs, MCPs, CLIs, and how systems fit together without a translator.
You've worked in a startup, not just a big company. You're comfortable with ambiguity, small teams, and owning outcomes end to end. You don't need a big-company machine around you to be effective.
You've built technical products, ideally developer tools. Adjacent technical products count. Experience in monitoring or observability is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
New to the PM title? That's fine. If you're coming from a founding or solutions-engineering seat and want to go all-in on product, we want to hear from you.
You're technical enough to be dangerous with AI tooling. You can prototype in code, throw together a mock, or pressure-test technical viability yourself when it moves things forward.

s.h: What you will hate about us
s.t:
We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.
We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.
We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.
We are lean, so you own the boring parts too. There is no PM ops layer to delegate the unglamorous work to. You will do strategy one hour and clean up a messy spec the next.
We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.
Customer signals come first, and most of the time they beat your gut. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up. Earn it by making customers happy, and then there is room for the moonshots. If you want to lead with your own bold bets, you will find this frustrating.

About MUBI
MUBI is a global streaming service, production company and film distributor dedicated to elevating great cinema. To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.
That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.

This is a senior, hands-on product role for someone who wants to own a meaningful slice of the MUBI product end-to-end, and is at their best when the problem is still ambiguous.
You’ll own the Audience & Platform Expansion domain - a critical product surface for our next phase of growth. In this role, you will be responsible for building the scalable foundation to drive global subscriber acquisition and pioneer our tiered premium offerings.

You’ll own its strategy, its roadmap and its delivery, from a high-level business goal all the way to a shipped, measured feature. The hardest product problems at MUBI cross team and time-zone boundaries, and break down without someone holding the whole picture; this role exists to be that person for one of these domains.
Reporting to our Senior Product Director, this is a senior, individual contributor role. You'll lead through clarity and influence rather than headcount - aligning engineering, design and data scientists around a vision they actually believe in, and mentoring/coaching other, more junior PMs as you go. We care about craft, in the films we champion and in the products we build, so the bar is product excellence and real user impact, not shipping for its own sake.
We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in Soho, London (if you're in commutable distance from London). Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.
Where you'll have impact
You'll own a product surface that leadership relies on, translating ambiguous, evolving priorities into a roadmap teams can execute against - and giving the business a crisp, honest read on what's working, what isn't, and what needs a decision. As you build credibility through delivery, you'll set the standard for how product strategy is articulated and defended at MUBI. Concretely, you'll:
Translate business goals into clear, actionable product roadmaps, and own the sub-strategy for a specific MUBI area (e.g. onboarding, content/catalogue discovery, monetization, or viewer experience).
Guide technical products through the entire lifecycle - from conception, through development, into launch - and iterate after.
Partner directly with Engineering, UX/UI Design, Data Science, Marketing, Business Development and Legal to define product requirements and resolve trade-offs.
Establish the KPIs and OKRs for your area, and use data-backed insight to iterate quickly and demonstrate measurable impact.
Pitch roadmaps to senior leadership to guide resource allocation, and align engineering, design and analytics teams without relying on direct hierarchy.
Write narrative strategy memos and present complex visions clearly - to senior leadership and engineering teams alike.
Mentor other team members and raise the bar for product thinking around you.

You've spent significant time shipping complex technical products end to end, and you're happiest owning a problem from the messy, ambiguous start rather than picking up a tidy backlog. You bring structure where there is none - a clear strategy, sharp prioritisation, honest measurement - without becoming a source of process for its own sake.
You're technically fluent enough to hold your own with strong engineers: you can translate an ML model, a streaming architecture or a latency constraint into a business trade-off a stakeholder can act on, and tell a real architectural limit from a convenient one.
You're an excellent communicator who can flex between an engineer and an executive in the same hour, equally comfortable writing a strategy memo and defending it in a leadership review.
You lead through influence - aligning people across functions, regions and time zones around work they want to do.

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Design, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years in product management or a closely related technical role, with at least 3–5 years focused on shipping complex technical products from 0 to 1.
Strong business judgment and strategic thinking - able to see the big picture and make connections across teams and issues.
Technical acumen: the ability to translate highly technical engineering constraints (machine learning models, streaming architectures, latency) into clear business trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders.
Deep domain fluency in identity and access management, subscription management, billing and monetization, and data processing - with the ability to debate architectural and technical trade-offs.
A proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through influence rather than direct authority.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including narrative strategy writing for senior audiences.
Strong problem-solving, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Experience with AI tools, and AI prototyping
A deep alignment with MUBI's culture and values: craftsmanship, product excellence, a bias toward high-impact work, and genuine respect for the user.

We are looking for a Product Operations for Latin America to own how new currencies and corridors actually get to market across the region. Every currency we launch unlocks new corridors for our institutional clients and drives trading volume and revenue directly.

Your mandate is to make that expansion happen on the ground: sourcing and onboarding liquidity providers, standing up settlement rails with banking partners, clearing jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements, and holding every launch to the reliability bar our clients expect.
You will run the regional launch pipeline with real independence. You will own pricing inputs, sequencing and the go-live decision. You report to the Product Leader of Global Payments & Currencies, who sets strategic prioritisation for which currencies matter most based on payout corridor relevance. You own the how and the when.
If you have shipped cross-border payment products, worked with banking or card network infrastructure, or built API-driven financial products across jurisdictions, this role will feel familiar. The difference is that you will be doing it at the frontier of stablecoin-settled FX infrastructure, where the rails are new and the playbook is yours to write.

Own corridor launch, end to end. You own every currency in your regional pipeline from Alpha through General Availability. You track liquidity partner onboarding, settlement rail readiness, regulatory clearance, operational setup and pricing. You run readiness reviews, maintain the launch checklist, and make the go/no-go call.
Operationalise our licences. Holding a licence and being able to use it are two different things. You work with Product Management, Legal and Regulatory, Compliance, Finance and Engineering to turn each licence, registration and partner permission into permitted product scope, documented operating procedures and live client flows.

You keep what we are authorised to do and what we actually run in market in step, and you make sure new capability reaches clients as soon as the licence allows rather than months later.
Work directly with LPs and banking partners. You are the product voice in liquidity provider onboarding and banking partner discussions. You understand what it takes to stand up a new currency pair technically, what banking partners need in order to enable settlement, and how to translate partner constraints into product decisions.
Navigate multi-market regulatory complexity. Every currency carries jurisdiction-specific requirements. You work with Legal and Regulatory to establish what is needed, translate it into product and engineering decisions, and ensure no currency launches without clearance.
Prioritise engineering effort. You work with engineers to deliver against the roadmap. You write specs, set sprint priorities, and partner with your EM so capacity lands on the highest-impact currencies.
Drive post-launch adoption. A currency is not done at launch. You track whether clients are actually trading new corridors, partner with GTM to drive activation, find the friction, and feed what you learn back into prioritisation.
Build the regional launch playbook. You turn each launch into a repeatable, documented process covering every dependency, gate criterion and handoff, so the tenth currency is faster than the first.

Comfort operating between product, legal and compliance. You can read a regulatory requirement, work out what it means for a product flow, and drive it to a decision without waiting to be told.
